title: Driftward Plateau
description: An asymmetric faulted limestone island with a long keel, detached fragments and a grass-capped summit. The keel starts near Z=0.

review.notes: New budget round 2: rejected. Fixed: the ledge soffits are now broken, dripping undersides of varied depth instead of flat trays; the keel ends in a blunt broken tip instead of a needle; the stray plate and the black rim wedge are gone; the cliff faces have crisp fracture planes between darker vertical joints; hanging grass runs along the turf rim (closeup, closeup_base, turn tiles). Still failing: (1) material/defects 7: the soffit undersides render pale cream-yellow, lighter and warmer than the grey cliff faces, with smeared, stretched texture and thin black zigzag hairlines across them (closeup_base upper left and centre). (2) form_detail 7: the keel tip ends in large flat, untextured clean slabs (closeup_base lower centre), and the cliff faces are one even scale of small cubic facets, like crumpled low-poly paper, with no larger bed planes between the joints (closeup bottom). (3) defects 7: the turf still meets the rock along a hard thin dark line with no visible soil band (the roots are too thin to read at any review distance), with small white specks along the seam; the meadow rocks are flat-faced low-poly prisms; the satellite in turn_067 is a lone faceted cube. Fix: give the soffits the same grey limestone material and texture scale as the faces with proper mapping (no stretch, no black lines); break the keel tip slabs with fractures and texture; add a larger bed-plane scale to the faces; show a 0.3-0.8 m dark soil band with visible root strands under the turf lip; round and fracture the meadow rocks; give the cube satellite a turf cap or remove it.
